findings.area: secret / provider transport boundary (credential forwarded across an HTTP redirect)
findings.summary: RESOLVED, re-verified by this reviewer against the SHIPPED assembly rather than by trusting the task reports. All four named provider clients resolve, after unwrapping the full IHttpClientFactory handler chain, to an HttpClientHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=False wrapping a SocketsHttpHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=False; the two opt-in .Insecure names additionally carry HttpClientHandler.DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator and the two strict names do not, so the strict/insecure certificate split is preserved. The .NET factory default primary handler on this runtime is SocketsHttpHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=True, so the fix changes exactly one effective property relative to the baseline; UseCookies=True, Credentials=null, UseProxy=True, AutomaticDecompression=None, PreAuthenticate=False and MaxAutomaticRedirections=50 are identical to the baseline. A reviewer-authored two-origin loopback reproduction using the SHIPPED SonarrClient and the SHIPPED SecretLease.ApplyTo confirms the credential does not leave the configured origin: the configured origin received 'GET /api/v3/system/status' with X-Api-Key present, the 3xx target origin received 0 requests, and the call failed closed with ArrProviderErrorCode.InvalidResponse / ArrErrorRetryability.Never and a fixed 93-character code-owned message containing neither the key, nor a provider body sentinel, nor a provider header sentinel, nor the Location URL. The same probe run against a bare AddHttpClient(name) control using the identical shipped client and lease code DID deliver the key to the second origin (key-present=True, 1 target request), which proves the negative result is attributable to the fix and not to a harness that cannot observe the leak. The 3xx arm is consulted before ReadContentAsync, so a provider-controlled 3xx body or header never reaches memory, a log line, or persisted state, and Retryability.Never means it is never re-sent.

findings.summary: RESOLVED, re-verified by this reviewer against the SHIPPED assembly. The task 21.11 fix replaced the Cc-only predicate (Rune.IsControl) with an explicit four-category predicate over UnicodeCategory: Control (Cc), Format (Cf), LineSeparator (Zl), ParagraphSeparator (Zp). I enumerated every scalar in those four categories across the entire Unicode code space (U+0000..U+10FFFF, surrogate range skipped because it cannot be a Rune) and passed each through LogSubject.Create in the 'A<rune>B' shape: 237 Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp scalars enumerated, 237 removed, 0 survivors. The specific scalars the 21.5 and 21.10 reviews reproduced as passing through verbatim are now all removed: U+202E RLO, U+202D LRO, U+200B ZWSP, U+200C ZWNJ, U+200D ZWJ, U+2066 LRI, U+2069 PDI, U+00AD, U+FEFF, U+061C, U+0600, U+070F, U+2028 and U+2029, alongside ordinary Cc (U+0000, U+0001, U+007F). A dedicated log-injection sweep confirms that no character capable of splitting, terminating, reordering, or colouring a log record survives: LF, CR, VT, FF, ESC, NEL, NUL, DEL, C1 CSI (U+009B), U+2028, U+2029, the bidi controls U+202A..U+202E and U+2066..U+2069, the marks U+200E/U+200F/U+061C, U+00AD and U+FEFF are all removed. The throttle still keys admission on category plus the code-owned ArrTagsLogEvent and never on the message, so a hostile name still cannot grow the 256-key tracking set or the log volume, and ArrTagsLog.Write still emits the identical {ArrTagsMessage} shape at every verbosity, so raising verbosity cannot expand a redacted value. The MaximumScalarValues=128 bound is still applied AFTER removal, so an attacker cannot pad the subject with invisible scalars to push the meaningful part past the bound: 10,000 interleaved U+200B/U+0001 plus a 22-scalar visible tail yields exactly the 22-scalar tail, and 5,000 visible scalars yield exactly 128. I could not construct any residual leak in this area, so the finding is closed as resolved rather than retained as hardening.

findings.area: log path disclosure / bounded log subject (ADR-026)
findings.summary: RESOLVED, re-verified by this reviewer against the SHIPPED assembly. The task 21.11 fix replaced Path.GetFileName (host-platform separator semantics) with ExtractFinalComponent, which takes Math.Max(path.LastIndexOf('/'), path.LastIndexOf('\\')) and returns the substring after it, so both separators are recognized on every host. The two cases the 21.5 and 21.10 reviews reproduced as leaking a whole Windows or UNC path are now component-only: 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv' -> 'secret.mkv' and '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv' -> 'file.mkv', so no user account name and no directory chain is emitted. I probed further for an escape and found none: the device forms '\\?\C:\Users\admin\secret.mkv' and '//?/C:/secret.mkv' both yield 'secret.mkv'; 'file:///media/movies/x.mkv' yields 'x.mkv'; a traversal-shaped '/media/movies/a/../../../../etc/passwd' yields 'passwd' (final component only, no parent component is ever emitted); a relative 'relative/name.mkv' yields 'name.mkv'; a bare 'name.mkv' is returned whole because there is no separator at all, which is the intended single-component contract; a trailing separator ('/media/movies/', 'C:\', '/', '//', '\\') yields the empty component and correctly falls back to the item identifier in D format, so no directory is emitted for a directory-shaped path; and a whitespace-only, empty, or all-removed path also falls back. Non-ASCII and decomposed names are preserved ('/media/movies/日本語/映画.mkv' -> '映画.mkv'). The fallback check is correctly re-run on the extracted component and again on the normalized result, so a name that reduces to nothing after removal falls back rather than emitting an empty subject. The finding is closed as resolved; the one bounded trade the fix makes is recorded separately as SEC-21.14-01 rather than held open here.

findings.area: log fidelity / bounded log subject (new in this review, consequence of the task 21.11 fix)
findings.summary: New observation, no security defect, recorded so the release does not over-claim. The task 21.11 fix deliberately makes two bounded trades, and I reproduced both. (a) Legitimate characters are now removed. The Cf category includes several characters that are semantically meaningful in real media file names: U+200C ZWNJ (required in Persian and Urdu orthography), U+200D ZWJ (required in emoji ZWJ sequences and in several Indic scripts), U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN (ordinary in typographic titles), and the Arabic number signs U+0600-U+0605, U+06DD, U+070F Syriac abbreviation mark and U+08E2. A file named with an emoji ZWJ family sequence or a Persian ZWNJ therefore renders in the log as its constituent scalars. This affects only the operator-facing log subject; nothing is disclosed, no boundary is crossed, no secret is affected, and the subject is still bounded to 128 scalars. (b) Subject fidelity for a POSIX name containing a backslash: '/media/movies/2024\Best.mkv' now yields 'Best.mkv' rather than '2024\Best.mkv', because the component is taken after the later of the two separators. This errs toward non-disclosure and the trade is explicitly disclosed in the ADR-026 implementation note and in docs/architecture/12. Neither trade is a security weakness; both are the necessary cost of a host-independent directory/full-path exclusion, which is what SEC-21.5-03 required. A third bounded residual is also recorded: a primary path with no separator at all, or a UNC share root such as '\\server\share', yields the final component, so a bare drive spec ('C:') or a share name can be the whole subject. Both are final components, contain no directory chain, no account name and no server name beyond the share label, and a Jellyfin item's primary media path always points at a file.

findings.area: log integrity / bounded log subject (globalization-mode independence)
findings.summary: New observation, no defect, recorded because it bounds the reach of the SEC-21.5-02 disposition. The task 21.11 predicate is Rune.GetUnicodeCategory, so I checked whether its result could differ between the invariant-globalization test environment used for this review and the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host, which has ICU available. I could not execute the shipped assembly with ICU loaded in this environment (every CLR_ICU_VERSION_OVERRIDE and unversioned-symlink attempt failed with 'Could not load ICU data. The residual uncertainty if that reading were wrong is bounded and one-directional: the worst case is that a Cf scalar survives, which is the pre-fix behaviour, never a new leak.

findings.area: state integrity / versioned envelope, quarantine vs discard, lifecycle fence, write-ahead publication
findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 0b7a260 (no State/, Artwork/, or Reconciliation/ file changed since the 21.5 review; git diff 2072ec1 HEAD -- src/ lists only LogSubject.cs). AtomicFileWriter writes a FileMode.CreateNew temp file in the destination directory, Flush(flushToDisk:true), then File.Move overwrite, and deletes the temp file on any failure, so a torn write cannot replace a good record. HandleInvalid discards a Cache record (delete plus Discarded) and quarantines an Authoritative one (StateQuarantine.TryQuarantine moves the file with overwrite and writes a 512-character-bounded reason file, never deleting, and leaves the original in place when the move fails), so authoritative state is quarantined rather than replayed or deleted and cache state is safely discarded. Records are capped at MaxStateRecordBytes = 4 MiB. PluginStatePaths validates both path segments. The envelope's SHA-256 covers only PayloadJson, which remains the already-accepted SEC-3 (corruption detection, not tamper authentication; local write access to the state root is already the administrative boundary, and such a writer could delete files outright). The v1.2 cursor, the lifecycle fence, and the write-ahead publication ordering are unchanged.

findings.summary: Re-verified unchanged at HEAD 0b7a260. findings.summary: New adjudication of the task 21.13 live verifier's open MEDIUM F-21.13-3, recorded here because the release gate needs a security disposition and F-21.13-3 is a live-verification finding about the plugin configuration save path. Two behaviours were observed live: (a) the administrator GET /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration returns the live provider ApiKey values in the body; (b) POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration replaces the entire configuration, so a partial or empty body silently resets every omitted field including both provider keys. From a security standpoint neither is a plugin defect. (a) is the host's own documented plugin-configuration contract: the plugin's declared PluginConfiguration is serialized back by the host's PluginsController, the settings page is written to prefill three type="password" inputs from exactly that response, and the caller is already an authenticated administrator who can read the same values in the plugin's own ArrTags.xml on disk. No privilege is added and no new secret surface is opened. (b) is a usability trap reachable only by an authenticated administrator acting on their own configuration, so it is self-inflicted; the resulting state is a valid empty-key configuration, not a corruption, and Plugin.UpdateConfiguration validates before persisting, holds one gate across validate/persist/activate, and retains the last valid snapshot and private secrets for an invalid candidate. I raise it as INFORMATIONAL rather than a security finding and recommend the verifier's documentation action, not a code change.
